newsitem.title: UK: Channel Island women embraced German invaders.
newsitem.headline: Channel Island women embraced German invaders.

text.p: The young women of the Channel Islands welcomed their wartime Nazi occupiers with an alacrity that horrified some of their fellow islanders, according to 50-year-old official British records published on Tuesday.

The intelligence reports say that huge numbers of the women of Guernsey and Jersey, whether married or not, had sexual relationships with Germans stationed on the islands during World War Two and that many were willing informers.
"The behaviour of a great number of women has been quite disgraceful," said one intelligence report.
One informant said the birth rate on Jersey never dropped during World War Two even though most of the local men were either serving abroad or had been deported.

"The Germans are taking the place of the potential British fathers who were evacuated in 1940," said one of the reports, kept secret until now because of the sensitivity of the Channel Islanders over claims they collaborated with the Germans.
Germany invaded the British islands in 1940 and held them throughout the war, even though they were of little strategic value, being closer to France than the British mainland.
The Germans met little resistance from the islanders, who felt they had been betrayed and abandoned by Britain.
Local businessmen had little hesitation about doing business with the occupying forces, while the islands' local rulers and dignitaries were accused of acquiescing to German rule.
Landowners were accused of discouraging people from fleeing because they wanted enough workers for their land.
But it was the women who were most castigated.
"Illegitimate births have been considerable and quite indiscriminate. The informant cannot think what can have come over the island girls," said one report.
One informant said there were 300 illegitimate births to foreigners in Guernsey, an island of 25,000 people, in 1943.
"At the present moment Westaway Creche is full up with the little bastards," said one informant.
It wasn't just sexual favours the local women offered.
One informant said he was jailed by the Germans after a Jersey woman reported him for listening to the BBC.
She is one of several women named as informers.
The Germans received hundreds of letters each week telling them of curfew infringements or ownership of radios, said a report, a symptom of the "moral rot" on the islands.
Some male islanders decided to take action against their treacherous women, forming a secret club called the Guernsey Underground Barbers (GUB) to punish them.
In September 1944, a woman informer was attacked "in either the eyes or the eyebrows" with a pair of scissors, it says in the only case it reports of the GUB's activities.
